Alex (Sales): Quick sync / Contoso procurement reached out: they need an executed MSA + DPA with EU data residency clause, plus a signed order form. POC team asked to extend to 120 days. Who owns DocuSign routing for EU deals? cc @Natalie (AE)
Natalie (AE): I spoke with their IT. They want SSO enabled and SOC 2 evidence before final signature. Also asked if the Dedicated plan can be reserved during POC. Procurement prefers billing to Contoso Ltd (Ireland) in EUR.
David (Legal): Looping in. Two immediate items: 1) Contoso submitted DPA redlines around subprocessors and a deletion of our export-control clause. 2) They requested removing Section 7 (export controls) entirely 12 we need their redlined document to respond. Please upload as .docx.
Sam (Platform Eng): Tech note: EU region + VPC private deployment is supported. SSO (SAML) onboarding typically takes ~2 business days. Reserved Dedicated for POC possible but ops requires a PO or refundable deposit for capacity reservation. Need to know GPU count/peak QPS to lock capacity.
Alex (Sales): Pasting their order form highlights here: ```
Service: Redwood Dedicated (eu-west)
POC duration: requested 120 days (they currently have 30)
Monthly commit: none for POC (trial)
Billing: invoice to Contoso Ltd (Ireland), currency EUR
Signature order: procurement -> legal -> exec
```
Natalie (AE): Procurement also asked about SLA credits during the POC 12 they expect 99.9% or credits. Can we provide SLA credits for a trial?
David (Legal): We don't grant SLA credits for trial/POS. I can offer a clarified POC SLA: uptime best-effort, no credit, reduced liability cap. For the DPA: I will not accept removal of export controls. I'll propose compromise language: keep export-control restrictions but allow customer review of processor list + 30-day notice for new subprocessors.
Alex (Sales): They pasted DPA excerpt: "Remove Section 7 (Data Export Restrictions). Replace 'restricted' with 'customer-managed oversight'." That would let them push keys out of EU. Not acceptable to ops.
Sam (Platform Eng): Correct 12 that section ties to our KMS/HSM requirements for EU keys. If they delete it we could be forced to host keys or backups outside EU, which violates our compliance profile. We need explicit export-control language in DPA.
Natalie (AE): Action items: 1) @David draft compromise export-control language and redline the MSA/DPA, 2) @Sam confirm deposit amount and capacity we can reserve for 120d POC with no commit, 3) @Alex collect final billing entity & signatory emails so I can set DocuSign routing.
David (Legal): I'll prepare annotated MSA+DPA and include suggested POC liability language. Draft will be uploaded as annotated PDF and a tracked-changes DOCX by EOD. If they insist on removing export controls we'll escalate to execs.
Sam (Platform Eng): For reserving capacity: Ops requires a refundable deposit of A320,000 EUR or a PO covering at least estimated hourly-run costs for the reserved GPUs. We can reserve up to 8 A100-equivalent GPUs for the POC. SSO adds ~2 business days.
Alex (Sales): Contoso procurement prefers procurement@contoso.com -> legal@contoso.com -> ceo@contoso.com as signing order. Can @Natalie confirm and I'll prepare DocuSign.
ops-bot: :information_source: DocuSign template for EU Dedicated orders: https://go.redwood/docusign-eu-template (use env=eu). Remember to set signing order and EUR billing.
Natalie (AE): I have the emails confirmed. I'll push Contoso to send the DPA redlines as a .docx so David can comment. Also confirming billing entity is Contoso Ltd (Ireland).
Alex (Sales): I'll tell Contoso we can do 120 days conditional on deposit or PO and accepted MSA/DPA redlines. I'll hold DocuSign routing until David's redlines are approved.
David (Legal): I'll include alternative MSA language around SLA for POC (no credits, explicit reduced cap). If they push, escalate to VP Legal.
Alex (Sales): Thanks all. I'll update the buyer at EOD with these requirements and next steps. :thumbsup:
